title: Classical AI
subtitle: Search, logic and probabilistic reasoning: the foundations of artificial intelligence
audience_line: University students in computer science and engineering
overview: This one-semester academic course covers the foundations of artificial intelligence: rational agents, search and problem solving, game playing, knowledge representation and logic, and reasoning under uncertainty and over time. It follows the structure of Russell and Norvig's Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach. Each part combines lectures that derive the algorithms with an implementation mini-project in Python, so that students both understand and build each method. The course closes with a capstone project: an AI system combining search, logic or probabilistic reasoning, proposed, developed and presented by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: University students in computer science and engineering

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Python programming (course: Python Programming Fundamentals); discrete mathematics and basic probability

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 90 h: 81 h of chapters + 9 h buffer, over one academic semester

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Lectures that derive each algorithm, followed by implementation mini-projects in Python

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per student with Python 3, Jupyter and VS Code; course code and datasets in a shared repository; no account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: Six mini-projects and a capstone project presented to the class; certificate of completion for students who complete both; grading follows the host institution's rules

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Students can formulate AI problems, implement and compare search, logic and probabilistic algorithms, and justify which method fits a problem

phases.name: Introduction & Intelligent Agents
phases.focus: What AI is, agents and environments, rationality
phases.intro: Students see what AI is, where it came from and where it is used, including its ethical questions, then learn the agent framework used throughout the course: environments, rationality and agent architectures. Mini-project: a simple agent designed and simulated in a grid environment.

chapters.title: What AI Is
chapters.content: Definitions, history, applications, ethics

chapters.title: Intelligent Agents
chapters.content: Agents, environments, rationality, agent architectures

chapters.title: Mini-Project: Agents
chapters.content: Design and simulate a simple agent

phases.name: Search & Problem Solving
phases.focus: Uninformed and heuristic search, local search, evolutionary methods, CSPs
phases.intro: Students formulate problems as state spaces and solve them with uninformed and heuristic search, local search, genetic algorithms and particle swarms, and constraint satisfaction. Mini-project: a planning or optimisation problem solved and compared with at least two search methods.

chapters.title: Uninformed Search
chapters.content: Problem formulation, BFS, DFS, uniform-cost search, iterative deepening

chapters.title: Heuristic Search
chapters.content: Greedy best-first, A*, admissibility and consistency

chapters.title: Local Search
chapters.content: Hill climbing, simulated annealing, local beam search

chapters.title: Evolutionary & Swarm Methods
chapters.content: Genetic algorithms, particle swarm optimisation

chapters.title: Constraint Satisfaction
chapters.content: CSPs, backtracking, arc consistency

chapters.title: Mini-Project: Search
chapters.content: Solve a planning or optimisation problem with search

phases.math: Graph theory (state spaces, paths) · Complexity (time and space of search algorithms) · Optimisation (objective functions, local optima, annealing schedules)

phases.name: Game Playing
phases.focus: Minimax, alpha-beta pruning, evaluation functions, Monte Carlo tree search
phases.intro: Students search against an opponent with minimax and alpha-beta pruning, design evaluation functions, and use Monte Carlo tree search when the game tree is too large. Mini-project: a game-playing agent evaluated against baseline players.

chapters.title: Adversarial Search
chapters.content: Minimax, alpha-beta pruning, evaluation functions, Monte Carlo tree search

chapters.title: Mini-Project: Game Agent
chapters.content: Build and evaluate a game-playing agent

phases.name: Knowledge Representation & Logic
phases.focus: Propositional and first-order logic, inference, knowledge engineering
phases.intro: Students represent knowledge in propositional and first-order logic and derive new facts with resolution, DPLL, forward and backward chaining and unification. Mini-project: a small knowledge base and reasoner that answers queries in a chosen domain.

chapters.title: Propositional Logic
chapters.content: Syntax, semantics, entailment

chapters.title: Propositional Inference
chapters.content: Resolution, DPLL, forward and backward chaining

chapters.title: First-Order Logic
chapters.content: Syntax, semantics, knowledge engineering

chapters.title: First-Order Inference
chapters.content: Unification, chaining, resolution

chapters.title: Mini-Project: Knowledge-Based Agent
chapters.content: Build a small knowledge base and reasoner

phases.math: Formal logic (syntax, semantics, entailment, soundness and completeness) · Satisfiability · Unification

phases.name: Probabilistic Reasoning
phases.focus: Probability, Bayesian networks, exact and approximate inference
phases.intro: Students reason under uncertainty with probability and Bayes' rule, model dependencies with Bayesian networks, and answer queries with exact inference and with sampling methods. Mini-project: a Bayesian network for a real decision problem, queried and checked against data.

chapters.title: Uncertainty & Probability
chapters.content: Probability axioms, Bayes' rule, independence

chapters.title: Bayesian Networks
chapters.content: Structure, conditional independence, semantics

chapters.title: Exact Inference
chapters.content: Enumeration, variable elimination

chapters.title: Approximate Inference
chapters.content: Sampling, likelihood weighting, MCMC

chapters.title: Mini-Project: Bayesian Network
chapters.content: Model and query a real decision problem

phases.math: Probability (axioms, conditional probability, Bayes' rule, independence) · Sampling and Markov chain Monte Carlo

phases.name: Reasoning over Time
phases.focus: Markov processes, hidden Markov models, filtering, smoothing, Viterbi
phases.intro: Students model processes that change over time with Markov chains and hidden Markov models, and infer hidden states with filtering, smoothing and the Viterbi algorithm. Mini-project: sequence labelling or tracking with a hidden Markov model.

chapters.title: Temporal Models & HMMs
chapters.content: Markov processes, hidden Markov models

chapters.title: Inference over Time
chapters.content: Filtering, smoothing, Viterbi

chapters.title: Mini-Project: HMM
chapters.content: Sequence labelling or tracking with an HMM

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A capstone AI system, proposed, developed and presented
phases.intro: Teams of two or three propose and build an AI system that combines at least two parts of the course, reusing their mini-projects, then present it to the class.

chapters.title: Proposal & Design
chapters.content: Problem statement, choice of methods, design and evaluation plan, approved by the lecturer

chapters.title: Development
chapters.content: Implementation and experiments

chapters.title: Evaluation & Report
chapters.content: Results, comparison with a baseline, written report

chapters.title: Presentation
chapters.content: Presentation to the class; questions and feedback

project.title: Capstone AI System
project.brief: An AI system that combines search, logic or probabilistic reasoning to solve a problem chosen by the team, evaluated against a baseline and explained in a written report.
project.stack: Python 3, Jupyter, NumPy, standard AI libraries where appropriate
project.deliverable: Proposal, code repository, written report, presentation
